open_points.subject: Registry storage boundary
open_points.text: “Registry stores identity and pointers only” conflicts with the Customer contact data, project status and timestamps, and artifact version/status that the same text requires Registry to store.
open_points.question: Is “identity and pointers only” meant to include all Registry-owned customer and lifecycle metadata, or must the storage promise be narrowed to enumerate the non-pointer facts Registry stores?
options: Treat customer contact and lifecycle metadata as Registry-owned catalogue data permitted by the promise
Restrict storage literally to project identity and artifact references
open_points.default_guess: Treat the explicit Customer, status, timestamp and version requirements as authoritative and narrow the phrase “identity and pointers only”.

open_points.subject: Service writes to Registry identity
open_points.text: “Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity and reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back” conflicts with Cabinet Kernel being allowed to create projects and add rooms, both of which write Registry-owned identity.
open_points.question: What does “none of them writes it back” prohibit: all service writes to project identity, only corrections of an existing snapshot, or something else?
options: Services may create projects and rooms but may not correct identity from their snapshots
Only staff may write project identity
The explicit per-action permissions override the blanket statement
open_points.default_guess: Allow the explicitly promised service create/add-room actions and interpret “writes it back” as prohibiting correction of identity from a consumer snapshot.

open_points.subject: Unauthenticated network boundary
open_points.text: “They reach Registry over HTTP on the host's loopback or private network” and “Reads ... stay open on loopback and the private network” do not define what counts as the private network or who establishes that boundary.
open_points.question: Which interfaces, peers or network controls form the trusted private-network boundary on which unauthenticated reads are allowed?
options: Loopback only unless an operator explicitly enables a named private interface
A deployment-defined network enforced by firewall or proxy
open_points.default_guess: Bind to loopback by default and require an explicit deployment configuration for any private-network interface.

open_points.subject: Credential configuration and administration
open_points.text: “service tokens and the staff credential, in the instance's protected configuration” leaves “protected configuration” abstract and names no actor responsible for provisioning, associating, rotating or revoking credentials.
open_points.question: What external configuration system holds credentials, and which actor is authorized to provision, rotate and revoke the staff credential and service tokens?
options: Deployment operator manages them out of band in environment or secret files
An external secret manager supplies them
open_points.default_guess: Use deployment-managed protected configuration with an administrator acting out of band and no credential-management API.

open_points.subject: Artifact vocabulary administration
open_points.text: “The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are a list in the instance's configuration” says the list can change but does not name who changes it, how a change is applied, or the observable result or failure of that operation.
open_points.question: Is vocabulary administration an out-of-band deployment operation or a Registry action, and who is authorized to perform it?
options: A deployment administrator changes configuration and restarts or reloads the instance
Staff changes it through an authenticated Registry action
The vocabulary is immutable for the lifetime of an instance
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an out-of-band deployment-administrator operation applied when the instance starts.

open_points.subject: Project-create replay after customer erasure
open_points.text: “an equal replay returns the existing project” conflicts with “a customer reference that is unknown or erased [is] refused” when an existing project's customer was erased after the original create.
open_points.question: When an equal create replay names an existing project whose referenced Customer has since been erased, does Registry return the existing project or refuse the erased customer reference?
options: Return the existing project because replay detection takes precedence
Refuse because customer validation takes precedence
Return the project but mark the referenced customer as erased
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing project unchanged because the customer was valid when the project was created and the replay creates no new reference.
